findings.title: Cape and tails pass through the head and neck on the shipped fighters: the SKIN-04 fix exists only in the demo knight, and the runtime neither adds nor checks head/neck colliders
findings.detail: Round 1 fixed SKIN-04 by adding head and neck capsules to src/char/designs/knight.js:52-53. KAEL, ISKA and VORN (src/fighters/*/design.js colliders, e.g. kael/design.js:93-106, iska/design.js:116-129, vorn/design.js:332-345) have no head or neck capsule. createCharacter (src/char/index.js:150) accepts any collider list, and the rule exists only as a README sentence (section 6). ISKA's tails are pinned at the chest, and her d+heavy launcher (iska.rising_crescent, the 'backflip slash' in MOVES.md) throws them up through the hood and neck. VORN's tails enter the head and arms in down/ko. The knight itself is fixed: at combo3@0.8 no cloth vertex is inside the helmet, against 101 in round 1. Repro: node tools/shot.mjs rigaudit_r2a --eval "__ED.r2a.scan('iska',['iska.rising_crescent'])".
findings.evidence:
r2a scan (rendered cloth vertices CPU-skinned like the GPU, inside body cores fitted to the plate and suit geometry; validated against SkinnedMesh.getVertexPosition, 1926 vs 1928 vertices):
- iska.rising_crescent: 152 tail vertices in the neck/head cores at t=0.5167, 46 mm deep, 17 frames. Held frame: 134-137 head vertices.
- vorn.down: 27 tail vertices in the head core, 40 mm.
- vorn.ko: 11 in the head; 30 tail vertices in the left upper arm, 89 mm, 192 frames.
- Knight combo3@0.8: 0 in the helmet (round 1: 177 vertices, 101 in the helmet).
Captures:
- shots/char/rig/r2a_cloth_body_sheet.png rows 2 (0.033/0.050): the tails come out of the hood and cross the mask.
- Row 5 (0.117): VORN ko, a tail panel standing up through the chest and arm.
Raw data: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user--/8256de2b-7eff-573b-8afc-504b52b3c9af/scratchpad/r2a/scan_iska.txt, scan_vorn.txt.
findings.suggestedFix: In createCharacter, when design.cloth is non-empty and no collider named head or neck exists, derive default capsules from rig.P x K and log a console warning (head ~[0.01,0.07]->[0,0.16] r 0.12; neck r 0.06). Add a rigqa group that scans every registered fighter's clips for rendered cloth inside body cores (rigaudit_r2a scan()). The art teams should add the capsules to the three designs.

findings.title: The off arm passes through the torso during a grip-point crossfade (KAEL idle -> guard), and whether it does depends on the breathing phase
findings.detail: The round-1 MATH-03 fix makes the off arm blend in local space at the slower grip weight gw while the hand lets go (src/char/index.js:567-570 offArm slerp, 590-601 let_go). The two endpoint arm poses are valid, but the slerp between them has no body constraint. The elbow-out-of-torso cost only acts inside solveLimb, and a hand let go to FK is not solved. KAEL's stance grips the 'grip' point and his guard grips the 'blade' point, so the most frequent transition takes this path. The result is not stable. With the same clip and the same clip time, two runs gave 1926 vertices inside the chest and a third gave 0. The only difference was the breathing phase, which teleport() does not reset. So the grip solve flips between two elbow basins during the fade. Mid-clip cases with no grip change also exist: KAEL ult.cuts, VORN hitLight, and VORN idle, where the left forearm disappears into the torso. Those are authored targets inside the body, and nothing in rigqa or qa.js runs on these clips.
findings.evidence:
Chest-core test, validated against three.js skinning:
- kael.guard@0.1667 after a 0.08 s fade from kael.idle: 1926 arm plate vertices inside the chest core, up to 116 mm deep (elbowL 1101, foreArmTwistL 544, upperArmTwistL 283).
- Same frame held with fade 0: 0 vertices.
- Same fade in a later run with a different breath phase: 0 vertices.
- kael.ult.cuts@0.4333: elbowL 997 vertices, 121 mm.
- vorn.hitLight@0.1333: upperArmTwistL 562 + elbowL 610 vertices, 115 mm.
- vorn.idle@1.0: foreArmTwistL 166 vertices, 92 mm, in all 183 idle frames.
Captures: shots/char/rig/r2a_arms_tassets_sheet.png:
- 0.033: the left gauntlet sticks out of the gorget, with the rest of the arm inside the cuirass.
- 0.050: the same clip and time, no crossing.
- 0.000: VORN idle, the left forearm enters the torso.
- 0.067: ult.cuts, the left arm rooted inside the chest.
rigqa's crossfade matrix also flags idle->guard (upperArmL 607 deg/s, 20.5x the clip's own steps) and accepts it with its limit of 2 pops.
findings.suggestedFix: During a grip change, solve the off arm by IK to a world-space target that travels around the torso, for example a waypoint offset outward along the chest capsule normal, with the elbow-out-of-body cost active, instead of slerping local rotations. Reset breathPhase in teleport(), or exclude it from the IK basin choice, so results are reproducible. Add a hand/forearm-vs-torso-capsule check (qa.bodyCapsules already exists) to auditClip and to rigqa, and run it on every registered clip.

findings.title: Cloth stretch is unbounded: structural edges reach 5-10x their rest length, and sheets split around limbs (collision overrides the distance constraints)
findings.detail: In src/char/cloth.js the Gauss-Seidel distance constraints run first. Then pushOutCapsules moves particles out of every capsule inside the last iteration (line 345) and again after the tethers (line 353). Tethers only bound each particle's distance to its own column's pin (tether 1.04). Horizontal and shear edges have no strain limit. Collision tests particles only, so a limb between two particles pushes them to opposite sides, and the interpolated sheet spans across or through the limb. Nothing detects pinned particles that start inside a collider. KAEL's cape corner is pinned at chest [0.07,0.205,-0.17], inside the shoulderL capsule (r 0.13 + margin 0.03). Row 1 is pushed out, so the corner edge sits at 5x in every frame of every clip, including idle. Round 1 accepted 'sim cape stretch 3.7' on the knight.
findings.evidence:
Maximum structural edge length / rest length (r2a scan, 60 Hz):
- KAEL cape, edge cols 0-1 row 1 (rest 61.4 mm): 4.1-5.5x in 27 of 29 clips. idle 4.81, walkB 5.26, ult.hurl 5.48.
- ISKA tabard: 9.99x in frostline_step@0.233, 8.99x in glacier_pirouette@0.433.
- ISKA tails: 5.7-6.8x in roll, star_fan, getup.
- VORN surcoat: 6.62x in lightning_charge, 6.49 ninefold_storm, 5.74 arc_step.
- Knight cape: 4.04x in combo3@0.667. Knight tabard: 3.29x in combo2.
Rendered sheet through a limb:
- ISKA glacier_pirouette: 102 tabard vertices in the right thigh core, 64 mm.
- Knight combo3@0.583: cape through the left spaulder, 29 vertices, 76 mm.
Captures: shots/char/rig/r2a_cloth_body_sheet.png:
- 0.000 (cloth only): KAEL's front-left cape corner is a flat stretched flap under the fur.
- 0.083: ISKA frostline_step, the tabard flung sideways as a thin flat strip.
- 0.067: glacier tabard torn around the thigh.
findings.suggestedFix: After the collision pass, strain-limit every structural and shear edge (for example <= 1.15x with inverse-mass weighting), then re-collide once. Give each particle a collider mask that ignores capsules containing its pinned anchor in the bind pose. Add a segment-vs-capsule test on structural edges (edges through a limb). Warn at createCharacter when pinned particles or rest particles start inside a collider. Add a rigqa check: max structural stretch <= 1.3 on every shipped cloth and clip.

findings.title: Elbow flips (swivel basin switches) remain in 5 of 5 demo attack clips, more than the two frames accepted as 'known'
findings.detail: The arm swivel is chosen by a stateless global minimisation (src/char/ik.js:184-214, HYSTERESIS false at line 13). Near-equal cost basins switch from one frame to the next. The fixer listed only combo3@0.233 and combo1M as residual. rigqa passes because it checks helper steps against source steps, hand twist and swing, and grip; it never checks elbow continuity. Measured as elbow displacement per frame against fist displacement in the same frame (knight, 60 Hz). This overlaps the math lens; it is reported here because the visible result is a 30-60 cm elbow pop.
findings.evidence:
Elbow vs fist motion per frame (mm), r2a batchB:
- combo1 t=0.45: left elbow 284 while the left fist moves 3.
- combo1M t=0.100: right elbow 587 (fist 106). t=0.117: left elbow 565 (fist 313).
- combo2 t=0.200/0.217: left elbow 371/350 (fist 100/121).
- combo3 t=0.117: right elbow 394 (fist 128). t=0.633: left elbow 401 (fist 59).
- slam t=0.600: right elbow 210 (fist 143).
rigaudit_skin twistScan (setClipTime, no fade):
- Elbow jumps: slam 0.33 m, combo2 0.42 m, combo3 0.40 m, combo1M 0.59 m per frame.
- Upper-arm twist steps 175-179 deg/frame.
- Deltoid steps 32-90 deg/frame (combo1M deltR 90.5).
findings.suggestedFix: Add an rigqa elbow-continuity check: elbow step <= 1.5x fist step + 2 cm per frame on every clip. Make the swivel stateful but frame-rate independent: integrate the swivel toward the optimum in fixed 1/120 s sub-steps with a rate limit, or continue from the previous key's solution. Separately, fix the clip keys that ask for unreachable wrist and shoulder rotations.

findings.title: The clavicle assist added in round 1 sinks the cuirass into the spaulders (idle included) and pushes spaulders into the helmet; it exceeds its documented 24 deg limit
findings.detail: clavicleAssist (src/char/ik.js:336-366) runs inside every arm solveLimb call: clip IK (index.js:434), reachGrip up to twice (490), the per-state grip solve and the post-blend grip solve (512). Each call adds to the clavicle the previous call already moved. The spaulders ride the deltoid helper, a child of the clavicle, while the cuirass is on the chest. A depressed or protracted clavicle therefore drives the lames into the cuirass, and an elevated one drives them into the bevor. In the knight's idle the right fist target (0.98 m) is near reach and the clavicle depresses 13.5 deg with no shoulder key. Differential test: the same pose with both clavicles reset to rest.
findings.evidence:
Knight, rigaudit_skin cross test (batchC):
- demo.idle@0.5, clavR 13.5 deg: cuirass into right spaulder lames 55 mm (57 vertices) + 51 mm. With the clavicles at rest: no deltoid crossing.
- demo.combo2@0.233, clavR 22.7 deg: 98 / 87 mm, vs 62 / 46 mm at rest.
- overheadWindup, clavL 29.8 deg: spaulder rim into bevor, 242 vertices, 43 mm; helmet rim into spaulder, 102 vertices, 51 mm. At rest: 37 vertices, 41 mm.
- overheadHigh: spaulderR rim into helmet, 69 vertices, 35 mm (none at rest).
- demo.hit@0.067: clavR 32.9 deg.
README and ik.js state 'up to ~24 deg'; 29.8 deg is reached with no authored shoulder key.
findings.suggestedFix: Compute the assist once per arm per update, as an absolute offset from the authored clavicle (store the pre-assist rotation and replace, do not accumulate). Cap the total at the documented value. Do not depress the clavicle for targets below the shoulder that are within reach. Counter-rotate the spaulder lames' helper by part of the clavicle offset, or add a girdle-vs-cuirass limit to the assist.

findings.title: Round-1 skinning and armour fixes do not reach any shipped fighter: no hipJoint/thighTwist/elbowVol/kneeVol stations, no tasset follow; KAEL's tassets sit 8 cm inside the thighs in every frame
findings.detail: The new helpers (skeleton.js:45-49) and the knight's reweighted lofts are opt-in design data. All three shipped suits use the round-0 weights: kael/design.js:153,160; iska/design.js:184,191; vorn/design.js lofts at 88/95 (hips -> thigh directly; narrow elbowR / kneeR bands). grep finds no reference to elbowVol, kneeVol, hipJoint or thighTwist in src/char/kit or src/fighters. The tassets on KAEL (design.js:86-87) and ISKA have no `follow`. So SKIN-08/09/10/11 are unfixed for every character that ships.
findings.evidence:
Suit vertices within 7 cm of the joint (r2a volume, distance to the bone polyline):
- elbow150: VORN 2.0 mm from the bone (ratio 0.042, 10 of 60 triangles folded), ISKA 3.1 mm, knight 4.5 mm.
- knee155: VORN 3.0 mm (0.044), ISKA 5.7 mm, knight 14.2 mm.
- KAEL: helper scale on vs off gives identical numbers (no vertex is weighted to elbowVol / kneeVol).
KAEL tasset plates inside the thigh core (bind-inside vertices excluded):
- 289-432 vertices, 73-80 mm, in every clip.
- kael.idle: 309 vertices in 183 of 183 frames.
Knight (follow 0.55):
- 0 in idle.
- 125-215 vertices, 41-64 mm in guard / walk / combos / slam.
- ROM: sideLunge 90 mm, hipRot-40 64 mm.
Capture: shots/char/rig/r2a_arms_tassets_sheet.png 0.083 (KAEL idle, camera side: the cuisse cuts across the right tasset lames).
findings.suggestedFix:
Make the correctives defaults rather than opt-ins:
- kit.loft/loftPair inserts hipJoint/thighTwist and the elbow/knee helper stations automatically when the path crosses hips->thigh, upperArm->foreArm or thigh->shin.
- A spring chain parented to hips whose name matches tasset* defaults to `follow` of the nearest thigh.
- rigqa measures every registered design (ring, axis, tasset crossing), not only the knight.

findings.title: Cloth is frame-rate and slow-motion dependent far beyond its chaotic noise (contradicts the round-1 SKIN-16 '30 vs 120 Hz consistent' claim)
findings.detail: In src/char/cloth.js:290-291, dt is clamped to 1/30 and steps = dt > 1/55 ? 3 : 2. That gives h = 1/90 s at 30 Hz, 1/120 at 60, 1/240 at 120, and 1/1200 at 0.1x slow motion, with a fixed 10 iterations per sub-step (line 184). Constraint iterations per game second are 900 / 1200 / 2400 / 12000, so stiffness, stretch and collision behaviour change with frame rate and with slow motion, which every skill and ultimate uses. The contract requires dt 1/30 to look identical. Each run is compared with the 60 Hz run at equal game times. The chaos baseline is the same 60 Hz run with a 0.01 m/s^2 breeze.
findings.evidence:
Cloth particle deviation from the 60 Hz run, KAEL (r2a dtCloth, batchI):
- kael.sweep:
  - Chaos baseline: max 2.6 cm, rms 0.36 cm.
  - 30 Hz: max 44 cm, rms 8.4 cm.
  - Alternating 60/30: 27 / 5.6 cm.
  - 120 Hz: 82 / 17.5 cm.
  - 0.1x slow motion: 108 / 26 cm.
- kael.walkF:
  - Chaos baseline: 8.1 / 1.3 cm.
  - 30 Hz: 28 / 6.4 cm.
  - 120 Hz: 38 / 9.7 cm.
  - Slow motion: 54 / 15 cm.
- iska.rime_flick: 30 Hz 57 cm; slow motion 94 cm.
findings.suggestedFix: Step the cloth with a fixed-h accumulator (h = 1/120 s of game time, the same h in slow motion), interpolating pins inside the step and the rendered particles between steps. Alternatively scale iterations with h so the iterations per second are constant. Add a rigqa check: 30 Hz and 0.1x deviation <= 3x the chaos baseline.

findings.title: The elbow/knee volume helper balloons the outside of the joint by 26-46% without fixing the inner elbow collapse
findings.detail: driveHelpers scales elbowVol/kneeVol along the half-joint's X axis by 1 + 0.22*flex (skeleton.js:255-256, 267-268); index.js:993-996 applies the scale. That axis is the crease bisector, so the scale pushes the olecranon or kneecap outward as much as it pushes the crease. Linear blending still collapses the inner elbow. The scale is non-uniform and goes through three.js skinning, which transforms normals with the same matrix (no inverse-transpose), so shading is skewed too. Differential test: the same pose with the helper scale forced to 1.
findings.evidence:
Knight (r2a volume, batchB):
- elbow150, scale [1.52, 1, 1.19]:
  - Min distance to the bones 4.5 mm (4.4 mm without the scale).
  - Max radius 74.4 mm vs 56.8 mm (ratio to bind 1.46 vs 1.07).
  - Folded triangles 24 vs 20 of 101.
- knee155: min 14.2 vs 7.1 mm (helps); max radius 79.8 vs 62.5 mm (+28%).
- elbow090 / knee090: max ratio 1.26 vs 1.07 / 1.13.
Round-1 deferred: elbow150 axis ratio 0.036, knee155 0.023 (unchanged).
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the symmetric scale with an inner-side push-out: translate a crease helper along the bisector, weighted only on the flexor-side vertices, or use corrective offsets driven by the flexion angle. Keep the extensor side unscaled. If any scale stays, skin normals with the inverse-transpose.

findings.detail: Re-run of rigaudit_skin rom() on the knight with the round-1 runtime. These are the items the fixer marked partial or deferred; listed so they are not lost. The knight is the best case, since the shipped fighters lack even these helpers (R2A-06).

- Pass: hipRot+-40 0.904, squat 0.914.
Min axis-distance ratio:

- Hip: sideLunge 0.123, squatDeep 0.356, hipRot 0.39.
Armour crossings (mm, vertex count n):

- hugChest 90.

- fwd60: plackart into fauld 91.

findings.title: See-through holes remain on all three shipped fighters (the knight is fixed: SKIN-07 and SKIN-13 verified)
findings.detail: GPU test: a front-face mask render compared with a double-sided silhouette, plate and suit slots only. The cloth slot is excluded because it is double-sided via cutout. The knight now passes. The shipped fighters' geometry comes from the art kit (src/char/kit/armor.js pauldrons, rims) and from ISKA's tailored cloth panels (tailor.js suppressRigCloth + panelCloth). Both bypass the runtime's shell inner-wall default and the cloth rim orientation. rigqa has no holes check.
findings.evidence:
Knight (vs round 1):
- Full body 2.6 m: 7 / 1 / 1 px (front / 34 / side), was 300-2585 px.
- Cape edge close-up 0.55 m: 0 px, was 17,812 px.
- Gauntlet close-up 0.6 m: 69 px, was 3,589 px.
Shipped fighters, full body 2.4-2.6 m:
- ISKA 1359 px (yaw 45) / 349 px (yaw -30).
- KAEL 1027 px.
- VORN 363 px.
Visible at: crescent spaulder backs, pauldron inner rims, ISKA tabard side edges.
Capture: shots/char/rig/r2a_holes_sheet.png (magenta overlay).
findings.suggestedFix:
Runtime side:
- Add rigaudit_r2a holes() for every registered design and quality tier to rigqa.
- Let a design hand the rig its own cloth render geometry, so the rim / side-strip logic applies (the change tailor.js requests).
- Expose a kit helper that builds inner walls and edge strips for open plates.
Art side: close the listed open edges, or set side 'double' where appropriate.

findings.title: Per-character CPU of the shipped designs is about 1.4x the knight the CPU check measures; KAEL/ISKA likely exceed the 1.0 ms rigqa limit
findings.detail: The rigqa CPU check measures only the demo knight (0.747 ms). The shipped designs carry more cloth (KAEL 191 particles, ISKA 180 in three cloths, VORN 180; the knight has 143), all at 10 iterations, plus more springs (ISKA ribbons). Measured in the same run with the same method (mean of each frame's fastest replay, 5 replays of a 4-attack chain). The machine was contended (load 90-100 on 4 cores), so absolute values are inflated; the ratio is the reliable number.
findings.evidence:
Same run, mean of per-frame minima:
- KAEL 1.444 ms, ISKA 1.436 ms, VORN 1.026 ms, knight 1.031 ms (p50 0.9 / 0.9 / 0.8 / 0.8).
- Scaled by the uncontended knight value 0.747 ms: KAEL ~1.05 ms, ISKA ~1.04 ms per update.
- Two fighters: ~2.1 ms of the 4 ms desktop JS budget; 6-10 ms projected on phones (8 ms budget).
findings.suggestedFix: Run rigqa's CPU group on every registered design. Scale cloth iterations by sheet size and by quality.cloth on the mid / low tiers. Consider a single shared sub-step for all cloths of a character, with early-out of capsule tests by bounding sphere per cloth.

findings.title: FK forearm / hand twist has no limit: a 178-182 deg FK key still candy-wraps the wrist (the helper is continuous now, the deformation is not)
findings.detail: driveHelpers moves any FK forearm Y-twist into the hand with no clamp (src/char/skeleton.js:226-232); foreArmTwist takes 65% of it. Only the IK path clamps pronation (ik.js clampWrist). Clips authored by FK can still ask for impossible pronation, and qa.jointLimits is the only warning.
findings.evidence:
rigaudit_skin rom:
- foreTw178 and foreTw182: forearm ring area 0.309 of bind (round 1: 0.284).
- Wrist axis ratio 0.905.
- rigqa: forearm twist sweep 160..200 is continuous (0.439 deg/frame), so SKIN-02's flip is fixed; the hourglass is not.
findings.suggestedFix: Soft-limit the FK pronation in driveHelpers to the same +-90 deg range as the IK clampWrist. Report FK keys beyond it in qa.jointLimits.

findings.title: The toe tip goes through the floor when the toe-bend clamp saturates (steep tiptoe feet)
findings.detail: floorFoot bends the toe up until its tip touches the floor, clamped to 1.4 rad (src/char/ik.js:432). For a foot pitched onto the ball with the heel high, 80 deg is not enough and the tip stays below the floor. Nothing then lifts the foot.
findings.evidence:
r2a batchG:
- kael.pyre@0.9167, right foot: ball 0 mm, heel 199 mm up, toe bend 80.2 deg (the clamp), toe tip -33 mm.
- iska.rising_crescent@0.45, left toe tip -15 mm, toe bend 80.2 deg.
findings.suggestedFix: When the toe clamp saturates, raise the ball/sole target by the residual and re-solve the leg, or reduce the foot pitch. Add 'toe tip below floor' to qa.floor (it currently checks feet sole points only).

findings.title: Rendered cloth dips below the floor in lying poses (the floor constraint acts on particles, not on the rendered surface)
findings.detail: cloth.js:354 keeps particles at floorY + 0.6 x margin. The rendered outer and inner layers sit thickness/2 off the particle surface, bilinear interpolation dips between particles, and ISKA's tailored panels add their own offsets. Knockdown, KO and crumple poses therefore show cloth sinking into the floor.
findings.evidence:
Lowest rendered cloth vertex, world y (r2a scan):
- vorn.ko -17.3 mm, vorn.down -10.3 mm, vorn.tech -7.8 mm, vorn.getup -5.2 mm.
- iska.defeat -8.0 mm, iska.intro -7.5 mm, iska.crumple -6.9 mm, iska.crystal_procession -7.1 mm.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a floor offset >= thickness/2 + 2 mm (scaled by K) for particles, or clamp rendered cloth height in the vertex shader for slots that carry cloth.

findings.title: The regression suite only covers the demo knight with demo clips: every defect above passes rigqa 388/0
findings.detail: src/labs/rigqa.js builds its characters from knight.js (mk(), lines 38-55) and plays the 10 demo clips. No shipped design (KAEL/ISKA/VORN) and none of the ~100 shipped fighter clips are measured. The cloth group checks only cape particles inside the head capsule on combo3 (0 by construction, since particles are pushed out of that capsule) and NaN. Not checked: rendered vertices, stretch, dt dependence, elbow continuity, body crossings, holes.
findings.evidence: node tools/shot.mjs rigqa --eval "__ED.lab.play('all', { detail: true })" -> 388 passed, 0 failed, 66.4 s. Five checks are capped as [known, round 1]. The crossfade check flags idle<->guard (upperArmL 607 deg/s, x20.55) and passes with limit 2. Meanwhile the r2a scans of the three shipped fighters (29 + 33 + 41 clips) found the issues in R2A-01..07 and R2A-13/14.
findings.suggestedFix:
Add a 'shipped' group to rigqa that loads each registered fighter (registry / design.js + clips) and runs rigaudit_r2a-style checks per clip, with thresholds:
- rendered cloth in body cores <= 5 vertices / 10 mm.
- Structural stretch <= 1.3.
- Elbow step <= 1.5x fist step + 2 cm.
- Tasset / arm plates in cores <= 10 mm.
- Toe / cloth floor >= -3 mm.
- Holes <= 50 px at 2.6 m.
- CPU per design.

findings.title: Arm IK still flips the elbow 90-179 deg in one frame, on human-feasible targets too. MATH-04 and ANIM-05 are not fixed by their own measurements.
findings.detail:
src/char/ik.js:181-222 (solveLimb, wrist branch) picks the elbow swivel by a stateless global search: 24 samples plus a golden-section refine of swivelCost, with HYSTERESIS = false (ik.js:13). The search jumps whenever two cost basins cross.
- The fixer's deferral says this only happens for keys that ask for an impossible wrist. A feasibility test disproves that: random smooth right-arm FK motions inside the human range (shoulder flex -10..130, abduction -70..10, humeral rotation +-30, elbow 20..120, wrist +-25/+-50/+-15) are recorded and replayed as hand IK keys every frame. The weapon is reproduced exactly (0 deg error), yet the elbow still jumps.
- The off hand on a two-handed grip flips back and forth too. bestRoll (ik.js:113) picks the roll from the swivel, and the swivel then depends on the roll.
- The forearm-twist helper (vambrace) spins with these flips. rigaudit_math twistPops (MATH-04's own test) still finds 31 helper turns over 60 deg/frame in the demo clips.
- rigqa passes because its helper check subtracts the arm's own step, and no check measures the elbow swivel. The README's known list (combo3 at 0.233, combo1M) understates the problem.

Repro:
- __ED.audit.run('feasible',80,11) in node tools/shot.mjs rigaudit_r2b
- __ED.audit.run('realClips','kael'|'iska'|'vorn')
- __ED.audit.run('demoClips')
findings.evidence:
Feasible-target replays (no impossible wrist demand):
- feasible(24,5): 2 flips in 2856 frames; elbow jumped 300.7 mm in one frame while the FK truth moved 2.7 mm (traj 22, t 1.433).
- feasible(80,11): 3 flips in 9520 frames; 315.2 mm vs 9.1 mm (t 0.95) and 239.3 mm vs 8.6 mm.
- Real Kael proportions, 40 trajectories: 1 flip, 135.8 mm vs 4.8 mm.
- Weapon orientation error 0 deg in every case.

Real clips, frames with an elbow swivel step over 30 deg/frame:
- KAEL: 18 of 29 clips, 85/1781 frames.
- ISKA: 24 of 38 clips, 191/2127 frames.
- VORN: 19 of 41 clips, 50/2199 frames.

Flips where the key's wrist demand is in human range:
- vorn.haft_spin R at 0.150: twist -22, swing 40. Elbow went [176,1240,335] -> [198,1385,24] mm (344 mm) while the wrist moved 39 mm.
- kael.victory R at 0.467: twist 13.5, swing 73. Elbow rose 224 mm while the wrist moved 80 mm.
- iska.frostline_step R at 0.05: twist 6, swing 66; 154 deg.

Demo clips:
- 27 flip frames in 783.
- demo.slam R: 145 deg on the impact frame (0.633), which hit-stop then holds.
- Vambrace helper over 60 deg/frame 31 times, max 172.2 (combo1M R at 0.1). Real clips have helper steps over 20 deg/frame in 21 Kael, 25 Iska and 17 Vorn clips.

Capture: shots/char/rig/r2b_kael_victory_elbow_flip_sheet.png. Between 0.450 and 0.467 the right arm switches from elbow-down to elbow-up and the blade turns over in one frame.
findings.suggestedFix:
Make the swivel continuous and frame-rate independent:
(a) Derive the default elbow pole from a smooth field of the target hand orientation (elbow opposite the back of the hand), so the cost has one basin around the human solution.
(b) Or carry the swivel as state, advanced by a sub-stepped critically damped spring toward the cost minimum (the same scheme the flinch springs use, so 30/60/120 Hz match). Allow a basin change only after the current basin's cost exceeds the other by a margin for more than about 50 ms, and then blend over 0.1 s.
(c) For the grip arm, solve the roll and the swivel jointly with the same continuity.
Add rigqa checks on the demo and real clips and on feasible(): elbow swivel step <= 20 deg/frame and 0 feasible flips.

findings.title: lookAt snaps the head 120-170 deg in one frame during spins and whenever the target passes behind the head
findings.detail:
src/char/ik.js:445-476 (solveLook) rotates by the shortest arc from the current head forward vector to the target and caps it at 75 deg. When the target crosses behind the head, the arc's axis changes sign, so the capped rotation jumps from +75 to -75. Nothing smooths the look direction: index.js:977 only eases the weight.

The game calls char.lookAt(opponent head, 0.85) in the 'attack' state as well (src/game/actor.js:29 LOOKING, :200). Every spin move therefore snaps the head: Kael's combo3 finisher, Iska's Glacier Pirouette and Star Fan.

Repro: __ED.audit.run('lookSpin').
findings.evidence:
Head world-rotation step per frame, without look -> with lookAt([2.6,1.75,0]):
- demo.combo3: 20.1 -> 122.4 deg (t 0.483).
- iska.glacier_pirouette: 71.2 -> 168.7 deg (0.417).
- iska.star_fan: 70.9 -> 160.6 deg (0.2).

Target circling an idle knight at 2 deg/frame: head yaw -87 at a target angle of 180 -> +65 at 200. That is a 152 deg flip, up to 49.7 deg/frame.

Captures:
- shots/char/rig/r2b_combo3_look_snap_sheet.png: back of the helmet at 0.467, visor facing the camera at 0.483.
- shots/char/rig/r2b_combo3_nolook_sheet.png: same frames without look; the visor turns smoothly.
findings.suggestedFix:
- Fade the look weight to 0 as the target angle from the chest forward approaches the limit (e.g. smoothstep from 100 to 150 deg).
- Rate-limit and slerp the look rotation itself, frame-rate independently (exp(-k dt)).
- Keep the previous side (hysteresis) near 180 deg.
- Auto-release the look while the hips yaw rate exceeds about 400 deg/s, or have spin clips set look:false.
- Add a rigqa check: head step with lookAt on every demo and real clip <= 15 deg/frame.

findings.title: The wrist clamp silently overrides keyed blade orientations, no tool reports it, and the rig's gripAngle default of 0 makes it hit most of Iska's frames
findings.detail:
clampWrist (ik.js:302-329) bends the requested hand rotation into range. Two README claims do not hold:
- 'qa.jointLimits lists such frames' (README section 5, 'Arms stay human'): the clamped hand always sits inside the range, so jointLimits and the rigqa wrist checks (swing <= 87, twist <= 92) pass while the blade is 100+ deg off its key.
- char.diag has no aim or wrist residual, so a clip author cannot see that the hit-box and trail path differ from the authored one.

The gripAngle default of 0 (skeleton.js:130, index.js:45) makes this worse. The README says the knight needs 40, but all three real designs leave it unset. VORN's clip author works around it by FK-keying weaponR [0,0,-42] in every clip (src/fighters/vorn/clips/common.js GRIP_TILT); that breaks the day gripAngle is set.

Repro: realClips(fighter); realClips('iska', null, {over:{gripAngle:35}}). Metric: angle between hand*weaponRest and the keyed weapon frame.
findings.evidence:
Frames with a weapon key whose result is more than 10 deg off the key (and more than 30 deg):
- KAEL: 289/1772 (16%); over 30 deg: 105. Worst: kael.sweep 93.2 at 0.633, kael.lunge aim 78.2 at 0.233.
- ISKA: 1616/2097 (77%); over 30 deg: 1097 (52%). Worst: iska.ult.leap 153, iska.rising_crescent aim 120.5.
- VORN: 260/2140 (12%); over 30 deg: 90. Worst: vorn.ult.leap 167.6, vorn.thunder_javelin 101.5.
- demo.combo3: 110.7 deg at 0.25; demo.combo1M: 100.2 at 0.1.

ISKA with gripAngle 35: over 30 deg drops from 52% to 15% (318/2097); over 10 deg is 44%.

rigqa: all wrist checks pass (388/388).
findings.suggestedFix:
- Add char.diag.aimErr[R/L]: the blade deviation (deg) between the key and the result after the clamp. Add a qa/auditClip report of clamp activity (requested demand vs achieved) and a rigqa threshold.
- Fix the README claim.
- Take the default gripAngle from the weapon spec, or warn at createCharacter when a design with a weapon has no gripAngle.
- Document that FK weapon-tilt workarounds must be removed when gripAngle is set.

findings.title: Floor contact re-solves the leg with the default knee pole: authored knee poles are dropped whenever a planted foot is tilted, with a 159 mm knee pop at touchdown
findings.detail:
floorFoot (src/char/ik.js:407-411) re-solves the leg with pole null and soft 0 whenever the lowest sole point is 1e-5 below the floor. Any pitched foot triggers it: toes-down landings, standing on the balls of the feet, kneels.

The MATH-09 fix only passes the authored pole to the re-plant in index.js:932-935. The knee therefore jumps from the authored pole to the default 'knee over the toes' at touchdown and stays wrong while the foot is planted.

Repro: __ED.audit.run('floorPole'); scenario floorpole.
findings.evidence:
floorPole test:
- While the sole is 39 -> 12.7 mm in the air, the knee sits on the authored pole (0 deg off, knee direction 79 deg).
- At t=0.8 the ball reaches the floor (pitch -4). The knee swings to 51.5 deg off the pole (direction 26 deg): a 159.3 mm knee step in one frame. It stays 51 deg off until the end.

Real clip kael.defeat at t=1.5 (kneel: footR pitch -60, pole [0.2,0,0.3]):
- With the floor: knee 32.9 deg off the pole, at [62,210,459] mm.
- With the floor removed (root raised 1.5 m): knee on the pole, at [141,122,260] mm.
- So the kneeling knee is 9 cm higher and 20 cm further out than authored.

Capture: shots/char/rig/r2b_floor_pole_pop_sheet.png. Front view: knee out at 0.783, knee in at 0.800.
findings.suggestedFix:
- Pass the blended authored pole (final.feetPole) and the foot's soft value into floorFoot's solveLimb.
- Better: correct the floor contact by lifting the target along the leg plane while keeping the solved swivel. Re-solve with the same pole, or rotate only the ankle when the change is small.
- Add a rigqa check: knee-to-authored-pole angle <= 2 deg on planted pitched feet.

findings.title: Clavicle assist is applied up to three times per frame in two-handed grips, so the shoulder shrugs up to 46 deg (documented 24, human about 35)
findings.detail:
solveLimb runs clavicleAssist on every call (ik.js:153). With a two-handed grip, the main arm is solved:
- once for the clip IK (index.js:434);
- up to twice more by reachGrip (index.js:473-492).
Each call starts from the clavicle the previous call already raised, and the 24 deg softLimit applies per call, not to the total.

The off arm gets the assist twice: the per-state solveGrip, then the final solveGrip on a final.lq that already carries the first assist.

Repro: __ED.audit.run('clavicle').
findings.evidence:
clavicle() test, hand target overhead at a reach ratio of 0.8 to 1.3 (right shoulder angle):
- One hand: 1.7 / 15.8 / 23.6 / 23.9 / 23.9 / 23.9 deg.
- Same target, two-handed: 1.7 / 15.8 / 23.6 / 23.9 / 29.5 / 42.6 deg.

Real clips, shoulder rotation beyond the clip's own FK:
- kael.hitHeavy R 46.2 deg at 0.067; vorn.hitHeavy 46.5.
- kael.backstep 43.7; vorn.backstep 40.4; kael.vent 36.8.
- Clips over 24 deg: kael 12/29, vorn 13/41, demo 4/10 (demo.hit 32).

Capture: shots/char/rig/r2b_kael_hitheavy_clavicle_sheet.png. At 0.067 the right pauldron is raised to helmet height and hides the head.
findings.suggestedFix:
- Compute the assist once per limb and frame from the clip's FK clavicle: store the pre-assist clavicle and recompute from it in each re-solve. Or softLimit the total deviation from the clip clavicle, not each step.
- Add a rigqa check: shoulder deviation from FK <= 26 deg on all clips.

findings.title: Masked override layers miss their own IK targets by up to 44 cm (weapon tip by 1.6 m), and layer fades are linear
findings.detail:
applyLayers (src/char/index.js:653-654) resolves the layer clip, including its hand IK, on the layer's own pelvis and legs. It then copies only the masked local rotations onto the base pose's pelvis. The upper body therefore rotates with the base clip's hips yaw, and the blade and fist land far from the layer clip's root-space targets.

The README advertises layers for 'attack while walking'.

Layer weights ramp linearly (index.js:638-639), unlike the smoothstep crossfades, so they add a velocity step at the start and end of every fade.

Repro: __ED.audit.run('layerIK'); scenario layer.
findings.evidence:
walkF + layer('atk','demo.combo1',{mask:'upper'}):
- Weapon fist 438.3 mm from combo1's own hand target (t 0.483).
- Weapon tip up to 1606 mm from combo1 played alone. The previous auditor's tipVsCombo1 of 1.606 m at 0.35 is unchanged.

Fade start, same idle -> guard pose change:
- Layer (linear): 594 deg/s velocity step (foreArmL).
- Crossfade (smoothstep): 355 deg/s.

Capture: shots/char/rig/r2b_layer_over_walk_top_sheet.png. Top view at 0.30 and 0.35: combo1 alone points the blade toward -s, the layered copy toward +s.
findings.suggestedFix:
- After blending, re-solve the layer's hand IK (and grip) on the final skeleton, weighted by the layer weight.
- Or carry the layer's hips-to-chest yaw delta into the spine and chest so the root-space targets hold.
- Use smoothstep layer fades.
- Add a rigqa check: layered weapon-hand target error <= 1 cm.

findings.title: Looping quaternion tracks stall at the loop seam: rotation speed drops to 12-18% of mid-loop speed
findings.detail:
anim.js:180-187 aligns quaternion keys only with their predecessor, so the closing key (a copy of key 0) can come out negated. computeTangents (rigmath.js:209-212) then wraps the loop with values[n-2] and values[1]. Those are not in key 0's or the closing key's hemisphere, so the per-component slopes change sign and the tangents become 0.

Any looping rotation that turns more than 180 deg over the cycle hitches once per loop: weapon twirls, spear spins, wheels. The previous auditor's synthetic loopSpin result is unchanged.

Repro: __ED.audit.run('loopSeam').
findings.evidence:
- weaponR FK twirl, 360 deg per 0.8 s (450 deg/s wanted): 71-82 deg/s at the seam vs 377-469 mid-loop (min 71, max 626).
- Chest 0/120/240 loop (400 deg/s wanted): 53 deg/s at the seam vs 444-495 mid-loop.
- rigaudit_anim synthetic loopSpin: 27 deg/s at the seam vs 489-496 mid (want 400). keyContinuity reports no break, so the data check misses it.
findings.suggestedFix: In computeTangents for quaternion tracks (and the IK rot tracks), negate prev or next when its dot product with key i is below 0 before computing the slopes, including the loop wrap at i = 0 and i = n-1. Add the seam-speed check to rigqa: seam speed >= 80% of mid-loop speed.

findings.title: Planted feet that are out of reach float or slide 5-35 cm, and the pelvis drop exceeds its documented maximum
findings.detail:
Since the MATH-01 fix the drop is bounded, but nothing keeps an unreachable planted foot on the floor. Soft reach lifts the sole and the foot stops short of its key, so a 'planted' foot hangs in the air or drifts during walks and lunges.

The update-stage drop (index.js:918-921) adds a second pelvisDrop on top of per-state drops that are already at the cap. diag.drop therefore exceeds the README's 'at most design.maxPelvisDrop'.

The content is too wide for the hips (VORN's walk), but the rig fails in the most visible way and only reports it in diag.

Repro: rigaudit_math run('dropSweep'); realClips (metrics 'float' = lowest contact point, 'footOff').
findings.evidence:
dropSweep, rear foot 0.50 / 0.60 / 0.70 / 1.00 m behind the hip:
- Sole above the floor: 8 / 44 / 88 / 206 mm.
- Foot off target: 10 / 57 / 122 / 348 mm.
- Hips held at 880 mm (160 mm drop).

Real clips:
- vorn.walkF: whole foot 56.2 mm in the air and 80.6 mm off target at 0.167; diag.drop 181.8 mm vs the documented max 0.16 x 1.071 = 171 mm.
- vorn.walkB: 45.2 mm in the air, 51.3 mm off target.
- vorn.lightning_charge drop 178 mm; vorn.ult.lift 180.9 mm.
- kael.lunge: planted foot 160.3 mm off target at 0.333, drop 172 mm (limit 163).
- Drop over 5 cm in kael 10/29, vorn 12/41 and iska 1/38 clips.
findings.suggestedFix:
- Combine the per-state and update drops into one value before softLimit.
- When the drop is saturated, keep the sole on the floor: move the unreachable target horizontally toward the hip so the foot slides and does not lift. Report it in diag.footErr.
- In the lab or dev build, warn once per clip when footErr > 1 cm or drop > 5 cm, so the clip author fixes the hips.

findings.title: The rig regression suite reports 388/388 passed while all of the above fail
findings.detail:
src/labs/rigqa.js has these blind spots:
- stepAngles subtracts the source bone's own step, so a whole-arm flip passes.
- No check on elbow swivel, head steps with lookAt, layer target error, loop-seam speed, knee vs authored pole on the floor, accumulated clavicle, or aim residual after the wrist clamp.
- Real fighter clips are not covered at all.

The KNOWN list (2 items) and README section 10 say only combo3 at 0.233 and combo1M switch arms. The README also says 'qa.jointLimits lists such frames'. Both are contradicted by the measurements in R2B-01 and R2B-03. A green suite gives the 150-200 clip authors a false all-clear.
findings.evidence:
- node tools/shot.mjs rigqa --eval "__ED.lab.play('all')" -> passed 388, failed 0, 65.7 s. The KNOWN-capped checks pass at their caps (combo3 grip 0.139 m, combo1M helper 108.6 deg/frame).
- Same build: 27 demo elbow-flip frames in 5 clips.
- 326 flip frames in the real clips (85 Kael + 191 Iska + 50 Vorn).
- Head snaps of 122-169 deg/frame with lookAt.
- Layer tip error 1.6 m.
- Loop seam speed 12-18% of mid-loop.
- Clavicle 46 deg.

findings.title: MATH-08 not fully fixed: demo.combo3 hips acceleration is still 3.4x the authored value
findings.detail: rigaudit_math hipsJerk: every demo clip is at ratio 1.0 except demo.combo3. The automatic drop is released at the end of the spin through dropHold (index.js:900-907) plus the update-stage drop, and that adds a hips hitch.
findings.evidence: demo.combo3: actual hips 2nd difference 8.89 mm/frame^2 vs 2.63 authored at t=0.85 (ratio 3.4). All other demo clips: ratio 1.0.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply a single bounded drop (see R2B-08) and release it with a critically damped follower rather than a one-sided exponential. Add the hipsJerk ratio <= 1.5 to rigqa.

findings.title: MATH-20 only partly fixed: the toe-root ball pad is 4-9 mm under the floor on pitched feet
findings.detail: floorFoot checks the ball at [footLength, -ankleHeight] in the foot frame. After the toe bend, the toe bone's own sole point under its joint can still sit under the floor. rigqa measures different points and passes, so the fixer's '<= 1.5 mm' claim does not hold under the original measurement.
findings.evidence:
rigaudit_math toeRoll (round-1 measurement), ball = toeR [0, -(ankleHeight - footDrop), 0]:
- pitch -45: -8.61 mm.
- pitch -30: -3.98 mm.
- pitch -15: -1.02 mm.
findings.suggestedFix: Include the toe-root sole point (and the toe tip after bending) in floorFoot's lowest-point test, or bend the toe about the ball pad contact rather than the joint centre.

findings.title: External-time looping clips lose loop-boundary events and the wrap frame's root motion
findings.detail: advance() (src/char/index.js:336-355) treats a wrap under setClipTime (time < lastT) as a backward scrub. It emits nothing between lastT..d and 0..time, and it zeroes df/du for that frame. The game drives non-looping moves externally today, so the impact is limited. Any externally clocked loop, such as a game-timed walk, a channel or a stance loop, loses step and loop markers.
findings.evidence:
rigaudit_anim runtime.events (re-run):
- externalWrapEvents@60: e0 0/5, eEnd 0/4 (want e0 5, e1f 4, eMid 4, eEnd 4).
- externalWrapEvents@30: e1f 3/4.
- External demo.walkF over 3 cycles: root 1.058 m vs 1.08 m wanted (1.082 self-advanced).
findings.suggestedFix: In setClipTime for loops, keep an unwrapped external time (or detect a forward wrap when the new t is below lastT and the delta modulo the duration is smaller than half a cycle). Emit lastT..d and 0..t and add rootEnd for each wrap, as the self-advancing path already does.

auditors.verdict: On the demo knight, round 1 fixed most of what it claimed. The helper flips, grip loss overhead, the cape inside the helmet, scaled facing, giant offsets and see-through rims and cuffs all measure fixed (cape edge 17,812 px -> 0 px, gauntlets 3,589 -> 69 px, cape vertices in the helmet 177 -> 0). The deferred deformation items are still open: shoulder ring 0.63-0.82, elbow and knee collapse 0.036 / 0.023, spaulder, gorget and fauld crossings 57-118 mm. Two of the new mechanisms cause harm of their own. The clavicle assist sinks the cuirass 55 mm into the spaulder in idle and reaches 29.8 deg against a documented 24. The volume helper balloons the outer elbow and knee by 26-46% and does not fix the inner collapse. The decisive problem is reach: the fixes are opt-in design data, and none of the three shipped fighters use them. They have no head or neck colliders, no tasset follow, no new loft stations, and no inner walls or rim fixes in their art geometry. Their real clips show cloth through the head on ISKA's launcher, KAEL's tassets 8 cm inside his thighs in every frame, arms through the torso on the idle -> guard crossfade, cloth stretched 5-10x, and cloth that differs by 0.3-1 m between 30, 60 and 120 Hz and slow motion. rigqa still reports 388 / 0 because it only measures the knight with demo clips. Elbow flips of 30-59 cm per frame also remain in all 5 demo attack clips, not only the 2 known frames. For this lens the rig is well short of AAA. Make the safeguards runtime defaults: colliders, strain limiting, fixed-step cloth, helper stations, tasset follow. Then extend the regression suite to every shipped design and clip, before the next 150-200 clips are authored on top.

auditors.verdict:
The rig is not at a AAA standard yet for this lens. The math core is now solid: spaces, pelvis drop continuity, knee poles in the re-plant path, grip in real clips (0 mm at full grip), facing, scale, sockets, eases and the rapid-play cap all re-measure as fixed. The arm and head solvers are still not continuous, though, and the rig hides what it changes:
- **Elbow flips:** the stateless arm swivel flips the elbow 90-179 deg in one frame on human-feasible targets (5 flips in 104 random feasible arm motions). In the real fighter clips it does so in 18-24 clips per fighter, 326 frames in all, including impact frames that hit-stop holds. MATH-04 and ANIM-05 therefore fail their own measurement.
- **Head snaps:** lookAt, which the game turns on during attacks, snaps the head up to 169 deg in one frame in every spin.
- **Hidden blade changes:** the wrist clamp moves the blade off its key in 16-77% of keyed frames, and no diagnostic reports it. The rig's gripAngle default of 0 is left unset by all three real designs.
- **Knees and shoulders:** floor contact discards authored knee poles (a 159 mm pop at touchdown; Kael's kneel ends 9 cm above the floor). In two-handed grips the clavicle assist stacks to 46 deg.
- **Layers and loops:** masked layers miss their weapon targets by up to 1.6 m, and looping rotations stall at every seam.
- **Regression suite:** it reports 388/388 passed while all of this is present.

With 150-200 clips still to be authored for three bodies and a colossus, the swivel continuity, look-at continuity and an honest aim / clamp diagnostic in rigqa have to come first. The knee-pole, clavicle, layer and loop-seam fixes are local and cheap.
